findings.evidence: `upstream/TauCeti/.../Uniform/Basic.lean:109` `uniformMeasure_eq_zero_of_le (hba : b ≤ a) : uniformMeasure a b = 0`; `upstream/mathlib/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/L1Space/Integrable.lean:283` `integrable_zero_measure`; `upstream/mathlib/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/IntegrableOn.lean:101` `integrableOn_empty`. TauCeti's own file drops the endpoint hypothesis wherever the statement survives degeneracy (`integrableExpSet_id_uniformMeasure`, `uniformMeasure_eq_withDensity`, `measurable_uniformMeasure`), so the convention here is to omit it.
findings.fix: Drop `hab`: state `theorem integrable_uniformMeasure_iff {f : ℝ → E} {a b : ℝ} : Integrable f (uniformMeasure a b) ↔ IntegrableOn f (Set.Ioc a b)`, proving it by `rcases le_or_gt b a` (degenerate branch: `simp [uniformMeasure_eq_zero_of_le hba, Set.Ioc_eq_empty (by simpa using hba)]`), and then collapse `ContinuousOn.integrable_uniformMeasure` to the single application `(integrable_uniformMeasure_iff).mpr (hf.integrableOn_Icc.mono_set Set.Ioc_subset_Icc_self)`.
findings.issue: `integrable_uniformMeasure_iff` assumes `hab : a < b`, but the iff holds for every pair of endpoints: for `b ≤ a`, `uniformMeasure a b = 0` (TauCeti `uniformMeasure_eq_zero_of_le`) so the left side is `integrable_zero_measure`, and `Set.Ioc a b = ∅` so the right side is `integrableOn_empty`. The PR description itself advertises this lemma as holding "for every pair of endpoints". The too-strong hypothesis is what forces `ContinuousOn.integrable_uniformMeasure` (line 59) to carry its own `rcases le_or_gt b a` degenerate branch.

summary: The acceptance–rejection development is at the right level: the general measure lemma is proved first and every bound/probability result is derived from the hypothesis-free `map_fst_restrict_trialLaw_acceptSet`. One removable hypothesis: `integrable_uniformMeasure_iff`'s `a < b`, which also forces an avoidable case split in the lemma immediately below it.
